paper_records.paper_title: Nonlinear dynamic response of a wire rope isolator: Experiment, identification and validation
paper_records.repository_path: data/papers/verification/MP1-V002/2021-Nonlinear dynamic response of a wire rope isolator Experiment, identification and validation.pdf
paper_records.matrix_filename: 2021-Nonlinear dynamic response of a wire rope isolator Experiment, identification and validation.pdf
paper_records.why_added: Comprehensive mechanics study on multi-axis stick-slip friction in helical wire rope structures.
paper_records.threat_addressed: Threatens T1 by proving that multi-axis stick-slip friction in wire bundles is rigorously understood.
paper_records.method: Experimental dynamic shaker testing and multi-mechanism phenomenological identification
paper_records.material_or_system: Standard stainless steel wire rope isolator (WRI) with helical loop configuration
paper_records.loading_mode: Multi-axis dynamic excitation: compression-roll and tension-shear cyclic loading
paper_records.control_variables: Shaker base acceleration amplitude and frequency sweeps
paper_records.independent_variables: Excitation direction, displacement amplitude (0.5 mm to 10 mm), frequency (2 to 30 Hz)
paper_records.dependent_variables: Restoring forces, pinched hysteresis loops, dynamic stiffness, phase shift
paper_records.model_used: Phenomenological generalized Bouc-Wen differential model with multi-axis coupling
paper_records.constitutive_model: Nonlinear elastic restoring force combined with hysteretic friction displacement variables
paper_records.contact_or_friction_model: Smooth hysteretic friction formulation representing distributed inter-wire slip
paper_records.experiment_used: Tri-axial electrodynamic shaker testing facility, LVDTs, force transducers
paper_records.experimental_setup: Wire rope isolator mounted between rigid shaker fixture and seismic mass
paper_records.key_results: Demonstrated that inter-wire frictional stick-slip produces strong stiffness softening and high energy dissipation; validated that a 3D phenomenological model accurately predicts dynamic response under multi-axial base excitation.
paper_records.what_it_proves: Proves that inter-wire friction in helical wire ropes produces amplitude-dependent stiffness variation and dry friction damping.
paper_records.what_it_does_not_prove: Does not use shape memory alloys (steel only); does not apply active fluid confinement pressure.
directly_verified_statements: Inter-wire friction generates non-symmetric pinched hysteretic response under combined compression and roll (Section 3, pp. 6-9).
Initial stiffness is dominated by stick state, followed by gradual softening as inter-wire slip propagates (Section 4, pp. 10-12).
inferred_statements: Frictional jamming in wire bundles is mechanically equivalent to the stick-slip softening observed in wire rope isolators.
paper_records.limitations: Stainless steel only; phenomenological lumped parameter model rather than continuum FEA.
paper_records.impact_on_MP1: Demonstrates that friction-induced stiffness variation in wire bundles is thoroughly established in structural mechanics.
paper_records.evidence_pointers: Fig. 4 (experimental multi-axis hysteresis loops), Fig. 11 (model validation)

paper_records.paper_title: Experimental-Numerical Assessment of Mechanical Behavior of Laboratory-Made Steel and NiTi Shape Memory Alloy Wire Ropes
paper_records.repository_path: data/papers/verification/MP1-V002/2024-Experimental-Numerical Assessment of Mechanical Behavior of Laboratory-Made Steel and NiTi Shape Memory Alloy Wire Ropes.pdf
paper_records.matrix_filename: 2024-Experimental-Numerical Assessment of Mechanical Behavior of Laboratory-Made Steel and NiTi Shape Memory Alloy Wire Ropes.pdf
paper_records.why_added: Direct recent comparative experimental and numerical evaluation of steel vs NiTi wire ropes.
paper_records.threat_addressed: Threatens T1 and T3 by directly testing laboratory-made NiTi wire ropes under cyclic loading.
paper_records.method: Laboratory fabrication, mechanical tensile testing, and Abaqus 3D finite element modeling
paper_records.material_or_system: 1x7 laboratory-made steel wire ropes and 1x7 NiTi shape memory alloy wire ropes
paper_records.loading_mode: Quasi-static monotonic and cyclic axial tension
paper_records.independent_variables: Material type (Steel vs NiTi), helical lay pitch, strain amplitude
paper_records.dependent_variables: Force-displacement curves, energy dissipation per cycle, residual strain, equivalent stiffness
paper_records.model_used: Abaqus/Standard 3D solid continuum modeling with surface-to-surface contact
paper_records.constitutive_model: Built-in Abaqus Superelastic material model (Auricchio formulation)
paper_records.contact_or_friction_model: Surface-to-surface penalty contact with Coulomb friction (mu = 0.15)
paper_records.experiment_used: Universal testing machine equipped with mechanical wedge grips
paper_records.experimental_setup: Custom stranding jig used to fabricate 1x7 NiTi wire ropes; tested under displacement control
paper_records.key_results: NiTi wire ropes demonstrated superior energy dissipation and flag-shaped re-centering compared to steel ropes; 3D FEA with Auricchio constitutive model and penalty Coulomb friction successfully matched experimental curves.
paper_records.what_it_proves: Proves that NiTi wire ropes can be fabricated and simulated using standard 3D FE contact tools, confirming mutual wire slip and phase transformation.
paper_records.what_it_does_not_prove: Does not apply active transverse fluid pressure; tension loading only.
directly_verified_statements: NiTi wire ropes exhibit Flag-shaped hysteresis with minimal residual strain after cyclic loading to 6% strain (Section 3.2, pp. 8-11).
Abaqus 3D FE model with Auricchio superelasticity and Coulomb friction accurately captures inter-wire contact and axial response (Section 4, pp. 12-15).
inferred_statements: Commercial FEA tools (H0b) are capable of modeling multiwire NiTi structures without developing specialized coupling theories.
paper_records.limitations: 1x7 strands only; uniaxial tension only; no active fluid confinement pressure.
paper_records.impact_on_MP1: Provides direct evidence that NiTi wire bundles in mutual contact are established in 2024 literature and well-predicted by H0b.
paper_records.evidence_pointers: Fig. 7 (experimental load-unload curves), Fig. 12 (FEA contact stress contours)
